props.title: Syriana
props.initialSlug: Oil, power, and corruption collide in global chaos

sections.content: Syriana (2005) revolutionized political thrillers by weaving multiple storylines into a complex tapestry of global oil politics. Director Stephen Gaghan, fresh from writing Traffic (2000), applied the multi-narrative technique to expose how energy corporations, intelligence agencies, and Middle Eastern politics intersect. George Clooney's CIA operative Bob Barnes joins the ranks of morally compromised spies like those in The Spy Who Came in from the Cold (1965), while the corporate machinations echo Network (1976) in their cynical view of institutional power.

sections.content: The film's influence sparked a wave of complex political thrillers that tackled global issues through multiple perspectives. Babel (2006) adopted similar interconnected narratives across continents, while Fair Game (2010) focused on the real-life Valerie Plame CIA leak scandal. These films share Syriana's commitment to exposing how individual actions ripple through international politics and commerce.

Syriana's visual style - documentary-like handheld cameras and natural lighting - influenced later political thrillers like Green Zone (2010) and Body of Lies (2008). The approach lends authenticity to backroom dealings and covert operations, making abstract geopolitical concepts viscerally real through personal stories. sections.content: The film's examination of institutional corruption through multiple perspectives influenced later works like The Big Short (2015) and Vice (2018). These films adopt Syriana's approach of using interconnected narratives to explain complex systems, whether financial markets or political power structures. Even series like House of Cards (2013-2018) owe a debt to Syriana's unflinching look at power's moral cost.

What sets Syriana apart is its refusal to simplify complex issues. Unlike earlier political thrillers like Three Days of the Condor (1975) or All the President's Men (1976), there are no clear heroes or villains - only competing interests and moral compromises. This moral ambiguity influenced films like A Most Wanted Man (2014) and Bridge of Spies (2015).
